text: The owner stared at the note in wonder. <break time="0.8s" /> And he said that he could not change it. <break time="0.8s" /> But I could pay him any time. <break time="0.8s" /> I rushed back to the brothers house. <break time="0.8s" /> To correct their mistake. <break time="0.8s" /> But a servant told me that they had gone to the Continent. <break time="0.8s" /> Then I read the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> Which said that the money was lent to me. <break time="0.8s" /> For thirty days without interest. <break time="0.8s" /> At the end of the month. <break time="0.8s" /> I was to report back. <break time="0.8s" /> And if the writer won. <break time="0.8s" /> I would get any position I could fill. <break time="0.8s" /> The letter had no signature. <break time="0.8s" /> No address, and no date. <break time="0.8s" /> So I had no way. <break time="0.8s" /> To return the note. <break time="0.8s" /> I could not afford new clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> For I had nothing in the world. <break time="0.8s" /> But a million pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Still, I went into a tailors shop. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked for a cheap suit. <break time="0.8s" /> And a clerk named Tod. <break time="0.8s" /> Gave me one with a sneer. <break time="0.8s" /> When I handed him the note. <break time="0.8s" /> His smile froze. <break time="0.8s" /> And the owner of the shop. <break time="0.8s" /> Came running. <break time="0.8s" /> To see what was wrong. <break time="0.8s" /> The owner scolded Tod. <break time="0.8s" /> For selling a millionaire such a terrible suit. <break time="0.8s" /> And he measured me. <break time="0.8s" /> For the finest clothes in the shop. <break time="0.8s" /> I did warn him that he might have to wait a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> For his money. <break time="0.8s" /> But he said that he would gladly wait forever.
